---
title: "From Python"
---

```{python}
#| include: false
# Setup, hidden from readers. Every .qmd page starts with this same cell
# (tests/test_docs_pages.py checks). It works in a fresh folder, reads the
# example project from this repository's tests/data (offline), and defines
# sh(), which runs a command shown on the page and prints its output.
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import useful_views

_mirror = Path(useful_views.__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "tests" / "data"
if not (_mirror / "examples" / "pwt").is_dir():
    raise RuntimeError(f"no example data at {_mirror}")
os.environ["USEFUL_VIEWS_DATA_URL"] = str(_mirror)
os.environ.update(NO_COLOR="1", PYTHON_COLORS="0", COLUMNS="100", PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1", PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
WORK = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="useful-views-docs-")).resolve())
os.chdir(WORK)
warnings.formatwarning = lambda message, category, *args, **kwargs: f"{category.__name__}: {message}\n"


def sh(line, expect=0):
    """Run one command shown on the page (useful-views, cd or cat) and print
    its output as a terminal would. Fails if it exits with another code."""
    word, _, rest = line.partition(" ")
    if word == "cd":
        os.chdir(shlex.split(rest)[0])
        return
    if word == "cat":
        print(Path(shlex.split(rest)[0]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), end="")
        return
    if word != "useful-views":
        raise ValueError(f"sh() runs useful-views, cd and cat, not {line!r}")
    done = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "useful_views", *shlex.split(rest)],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
    )
    out = done.stdout.replace(WORK, "/path/to")
    if out.strip():
        print(out, end="")
    if done.returncode != expect:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{line!r} exited with {done.returncode}, not {expect}:\n{out}")
```

The functions in `useful_views` do what the commands do, from a script or a
notebook. This page runs the [Get started](../quickstart.qmd) walkthrough in
Python, as you would in a notebook.

The notebook must run in the environment useful-views is installed in. See
[Installation](../installation.md#in-a-notebook).

## Get the example

```{python}
import useful_views as uvs

project = uvs.example("pwt")
```

`example` downloads the example's raw data and recipes, checks each file
against its checksum, and sets up the folder as `init` would. It returns the
project folder, here `pwt-example/`. A second argument names another folder.

For your own data, `uvs.init("my-project")` makes the same
[layout](../concepts/projects.md), empty.

## Make the views

```{python}
result = uvs.sync(root=project)
result.ran
```

`sync` ran both recipes, upstream first. Its progress lines go to standard
error. A step's own output appears as the step runs.

```{python}
uvs.check(root=project)
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
assert result.ran == ("pwt_panel", "gdp_per_capita")
assert uvs.check(root=project) == []
```

An empty list means `check` found no problems.
[Run, sync and check](../concepts/running.qmd) says what each one does.

## Read a view

Views are parquet files, so any data library reads them:

```{python}
import polars as pl

gdp = pl.read_parquet(project / "useful-views" / "gdp-per-capita.parquet")
gdp.filter(pl.col("year") == 2023)
```

## Work in a notebook in the project

Save your notebooks inside the project, for example in `notebooks/`. Jupyter
starts a notebook in its own folder. useful-views walks up from there to the
folder that holds `datapackage.json`, so you can leave out `root=`:

```{python}
import os

os.makedirs(project / "notebooks", exist_ok=True)
os.chdir(project / "notebooks")  # Jupyter does this for a notebook saved there

uvs.check()
```

`uvs.root()` returns the project folder. Use it to build the path to a view:

```{python}
gdp = pl.read_parquet(uvs.root() / "useful-views" / "gdp-per-capita.parquet")
gdp.shape
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
assert uvs.root() == project
```

From a folder outside the project, name the project with `root=`, as in
`uvs.check(root="~/data/my-project")`. It is the folder that holds
`datapackage.json`. `new_recipe`, `run`, `sync`, `check` and `cookbook` take
`root=`. `init` and `example` take the folder to create instead. Outside a
project, `uvs.root()` raises `ProjectNotFound`.

On the command line, name it with `-C`, as in
`useful-views -C ~/data/my-project check`. See
[Command line](../reference/cli.md).

## Write a recipe

Add a recipe that reads the `gdp-per-capita` view and averages each
country's growth since 2000. Start from the template:

```{python}
folder = uvs.new_recipe("growth_since_2000")
```

`new_recipe` returns the recipe folder. It holds `recipe.toml`, which lists
one step, and that step's stub file, `01_first_step.py`. The descriptions
still say TODO, so running the recipe is refused before anything changes:

```{python}
try:
    uvs.run("growth_since_2000")
except uvs.RecipeRefused as err:
    print(err)
    print("rule:", err.rule, "| file to fix:", err.path)
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
try:
    uvs.run("growth_since_2000")
except uvs.RecipeRefused as err:
    assert err.rule == 1 and err.path == "recipes/growth_since_2000/recipe.toml"
else:
    raise AssertionError("the template recipe was not refused")
```

The message says what to fix, and where. `err.rule` is the number of the
broken [rule](../reference/rules.md).

Next you would edit the two files in your editor. Here Python writes them, so
the page runs as it stands. The step file is renamed `01_average_growth.py`,
and its `[[steps]]` block names that file. The paths in the step are the same
strings as in `recipe.toml`.

```{python}
(folder / "recipe.toml").write_text('''\
description = "Average annual growth of GDP per capita since 2000."
inputs  = ["useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet"]
outputs = ["useful-views/growth-since-2000.parquet"]

[[steps]]
file = "01_average_growth.py"
description = "Average the growth of GDP per capita by country, from 2000 on."
''')
(folder / "01_average_growth.py").write_text('''\
import polars as pl

gdp = pl.read_parquet("useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet")
growth = (
    gdp.filter(pl.col("year") >= 2000)
    .group_by("iso", "country")
    .agg(pl.col("growth_pct").mean().round(2).alias("avg_growth_pct"))
    .sort("iso")
)
growth.write_parquet("useful-views/growth-since-2000.parquet")
''')
(folder / "01_first_step.py").unlink()
```

`run` makes the one recipe you name:

```{python}
uvs.run("growth_since_2000")
```

```{python}
pl.read_parquet(uvs.root() / "useful-views" / "growth-since-2000.parquet")
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the text says; the build fails if it stops being true.
catalog = (uvs.root() / "useful-views" / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
assert [line for line in catalog if line.startswith("## ") and line.endswith(".parquet")] == [
    "## pwt-panel.parquet", "## gdp-per-capita.parquet", "## growth-since-2000.parquet"
]
assert uvs.check() == []
```

The catalog, `useful-views/README.md`, now lists three views.

## What the functions return

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `init`, `example` | the project folder, as an absolute path |
| `new_recipe` | the recipe folder |
| `run` | a `RunResult`: `recipe`, `outputs`, `warnings` |
| `sync` | a `SyncResult`: `removed`, `dropped`, `deleted`, `ran`, `reasons`, `warnings` |
| `check` | a list of `Finding`s: `kind`, `path`, `message`, `rule`, `recipe`, `reason` |
| `cookbook` | a `CookbookResult`: `path`, `written`, `up_to_date`, `recipes`, `findings` |
| `root` | the project folder |

## Errors and warnings

Every error is a `UsefulViewsError`. Each one has `recipe`, `sync_result` and
`to_dict()`, and the facts of its kind:

| Error | When | Its facts |
|---|---|---|
| `RecipeRefused` | a recipe breaks a rule, so nothing changed | `rule`, `rule_title`, `path`, `refusals` |
| `StepFailed` | a step failed | `step`, `returncode`, `stderr` |
| `OutputError` | a declared view is missing, empty or unreadable | `paths`, `problems` |
| `CookbookError` | the project isn't in sync, so the cookbook can't be written | `findings` |
| `ExampleError` | an example can't be downloaded or set up | `kind` |
| `DataHashError` | a file's [data hash](fingerprints.qmd) can't be computed | `path`, `column` |
| `ProjectNotFound` | no project is found | |
| `ProjectError` | the project is missing or damaged, or a file can't be written | |

Warnings are `UsefulViewsWarning`s. A notebook shows them as they happen, and
`RunResult` and `SyncResult` keep them in `warnings`.
